title: Escaping the Digital Unease / Raus aus dem digitalen Unbehagen

description.main: A bilingual book published with the 2017 group exhibition of the same name at Kunsthaus Langenthal. Essays on media culture and net criticism accompany the show.
description.extended:
The catalogue to Escaping the Digital Unease, a 2017 group exhibition at Kunsthaus Langenthal in Switzerland that asked what is behind the discomfort many feel with digital culture and how to get out of it.

The book runs in German and English across 144 pages and was published by Christoph Merian Verlag in Basel. It pairs documentation of the exhibition, held from September to November 2017, with critical and solution-oriented essays on media culture. Contributors are Raffael Dörig, Paul Feigelfeld, Claire Hoffmann, Marie Lechner, Domenico Quaranta and Felix Stalder. The cover credits Dörig and Quaranta as editors.

The cover names Kunsthaus Langenthal alongside the publisher, and the essays deal with net culture and the digital.

notes: A shelf list for this copy also names Fabio Paris as an editor; the cover credits only Raffael Dörig and Domenico Quaranta. The publisher link goes to the Kunsthaus Langenthal publication page. Identified from a spine photograph; edition not checked against the copy.
